mainTopic: The stages of purity after טומאה: טבילה for מעשר, sunset for תרומה, and the כפרה for קדשים, and whether someone who still owes a כפרה may eat תרומה.
overview: The גמרא finishes showing that the holy food in the פסוק 'עד אשר יטהר' is תרומה. Only תרומה is equal for all of אהרן's descendants: a חוזרת rules out חזה ושוק, and a חללה does not count as זרע אהרן. Then the גמרא asks whether 'until he is pure' means sunset or bringing a כפרה. דבי רבי ישמעאל answers that the פסוק is about people who never bring a כפרה, so it means sunset. The גמרא pushes further: maybe someone who does owe a כפרה must wait for it before eating תרומה. It also asks for the source of the משנה's three stages. רב חסדא answers with three פסוקים: טבילה for מעשר, sunset for תרומה, and the כפרה for קדשים. The order is defended by weighing which food is stricter, and רבא adds a proof from the word נפש. When the question about someone who owes a כפרה comes back, אביי proves from the two פסוקים about a יולדת that sunset permits תרומה, while קדשים must wait for the קרבן, and רבא backs this from the wording of the פסוק. רב שישא objects that a גיורת and a freed שפחה are included in that section even though they cannot eat תרומה. רבא answers 'ולא?', and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The holy food equal for all of אהרן's descendants is תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the holy food shared equally by all of אהרן's descendants must be תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which holy food is the same for all the seed of אהרן? You must say this is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its earlier question. The holy food in the פסוק, which belongs equally to all of אהרן's descendants, must be תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'any man from the seed of אהרן', which suggests a food every descendant shares, male and female alike. The גמרא identifies that food as תרומה. The next steps will test this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The seed (descendants) of אהרן, the כהנים and their families
You must say (this is the only option left)
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: for all the seed of Aaron, both sons and daughters —
you must say: this is terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation that began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The food equally shared by all of אהרן's descendants is תרומה.

steps.title: Maybe it means the breast and thigh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק could be talking about חזה ושוק instead of תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is the breast and thigh of a שלמים, which the family of a כהן also eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Male and female members of a כהן's family also eat חזה ושוק, so maybe the פסוק means them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If another holy food also fits 'all the seed of אהרן', the proof for תרומה is not certain. The challenge offers חזה ושוק as a second candidate.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (offering another possibility)
The breast and thigh of a קרבן שלמים, given to the כהן

phrases.english: But say it refers to the breast and thigh?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification of the food as תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the פסוק refers to תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חזה ושוק are also eaten by both males and females of a כהן's family, so they fit the פסוק too.

steps.title: A returning daughter cannot eat breast and thigh
steps.stepSummary: חזה ושוק are not equal for everyone, because a חוזרת may not eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The breast and thigh are not allowed to a daughter who returns to her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חזה ושוק are not truly equal for all, so they cannot be what the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's daughter who married a non-כהן, and was later widowed or divorced with no children, returns to her father's house. She may eat תרומה again but not חזה ושוק. So only תרומה is fully equal for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן's daughter who returns to her father's house after her marriage to a non-כהן ends

phrases.english: It is not permitted to the one who returns.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the breast and thigh. The 'one who returns' is the daughter coming back to her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from חזה ושוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing: the other candidate is not equal for everyone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזה ושוק fit 'all the seed of אהרן' just as well as תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חוזרת eats תרומה but not חזה ושוק, so only תרומה fits.

steps.title: But תרומה is not allowed to a חללה either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that תרומה is not fully equal either, since a חללה may not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: תרומה also is not allowed to a חללה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same argument against תרומה. If one excluded woman disqualifies חזה ושוק, then the excluded חללה should disqualify תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חללה is the daughter of a כהן who is disqualified from כהונה, and she cannot eat תרומה. So תרומה also seems not equal for all of אהרן's descendants.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
A woman disqualified from כהונה and from eating תרומה

phrases.english: Terumah too is not permitted to a chalalah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of the previous answer to attack תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תרומה alone is equal for all of אהרן's descendants.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חללה is excluded from תרומה, just as the חוזרת is excluded from חזה ושוק.

steps.title: A חללה does not count as זרע אהרן
steps.stepSummary: A חללה is not considered זרע אהרן, so leaving her out does not break the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חללה is not the seed of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a חללה is not part of the group the פסוק talks about at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חוזרת is truly part of אהרן's family and is still excluded from חזה ושוק, so they are not equal. A חללה lost her status as זרע אהרן. Among those who really are אהרן's descendants, תרומה is fully equal.

keyTerms.meaning: Not

steps.whatToRemember: Only תרומה is equal for all of אהרן's descendants. A חוזרת rules out חזה ושוק, and a חללה does not count as אהרן's seed.

phrases.english: A chalalah is not the seed of Aaron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חללה challenge and secures the identification as תרומה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the group: the excluded person is not part of the category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חללה is one of אהרן's descendants who cannot eat תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חללה is not counted as זרע אהרן, so תרומה stays equal for everyone in the group.

steps.title: Maybe 'until he is pure' means until he brings his offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know 'עד אשר יטהר' means sunset and not bringing a כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that 'until he is pure' means until sunset? Maybe it means until he brings his atonement offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. It questions whether 'until he is pure' really allows eating תרומה after sunset, before the person brings his קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא taught that someone still missing his atonement offering may eat תרומה. That only works if 'pure' means after sunset. The גמרא suggests 'pure' could mean fully finished, after bringing the כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
Until he becomes pure (ויקרא 22:4)
Sunset, which ends the day of טבילה
The atonement offering some טמאים must bring

phrases.english: And from where do we know that this 'until he is pure'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4

phrases.english: means until there is sunset?
Say: until he brings atonement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which food the פסוק means to what 'pure' means.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'עד אשר יטהר' means sunset, which lets someone still missing his offering eat תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Pure' could mean full purity, after bringing the כפרה.

steps.title: The verse is about people who never bring an offering
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that the פסוק speaks of a זב with two sightings and a מצורע מוסגר, who bring no כפרה, like a טמא נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be. The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: the פסוק speaks of a זב who had two sightings and a מצורע who was only quarantined. They are like a טמא נפש. Just as a טמא נפש does not bring a כפרה, these also do not bring a כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the people in this פסוק never bring a קרבן, so 'until he is pure' cannot mean until the offering. It must mean sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב with only two sightings and a מצורע מוסגר are טמא but bring no קרבן. The same פסוק mentions a טמא נפש, who also brings none. Since these people have no כפרה to wait for, their purity is complete at sunset.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible
A תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל taught
A זב who had only two emissions, so he is טמא but brings no קרבן
A suspected מצורע who is quarantined but not yet declared a full מצורע
Someone made טמא by contact with a dead body
Similar to, comparable to

steps.whatToRemember: 'עד אשר יטהר' means sunset. The פסוק speaks of people who never bring a כפרה, like a טמא נפש, so waiting for an offering cannot be what it means.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say a זב or מצורע never brings a קרבן. A זב with three sightings and a confirmed מצורע do bring one. This פסוק is only about the lighter cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once 'pure' means sunset, the פסוק shows that טבילה and sunset are enough for תרומה. This supports the ברייתא's ruling that someone still missing his atonement may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: This cannot enter your mind,
as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
about a zav who had two sightings
phrases.notes: Two sightings make him טמא, but only a third one would require a קרבן.

phrases.english: and about a quarantined leper the verse is speaking,
similar to 'impure by a corpse',
phrases.notes: This comes from later in the same פסוק: 'one who touches anything טמא נפש' (ויקרא 22:4).

phrases.aramaic: מָה ״טְמֵא נֶפֶשׁ״ דְּלָאו בַּר כַּפָּרָה הוּא —
phrases.english: just as one impure by a corpse does not require atonement —

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי נָמֵי דְּלָאו בְּנֵי כַּפָּרָה נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: these too are ones who do not require atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that 'pure' might mean bringing a כפרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the people in the פסוק never bring a כפרה, proven by comparing them to the טמא נפש in the same פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until he is pure' might mean until he brings his atonement offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks of a זב with two sightings and a מצורע מוסגר, who bring no כפרה, so 'pure' means sunset.

steps.title: Maybe sunset is enough only for someone who brings no atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 7: the פסוק may only teach about people who bring no כפרה, but someone who must bring a כפרה might have to wait for it before eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you could say: this rule, that sunset is enough, applies only to someone who does not need to bring a כפרה. But someone who does need a כפרה cannot eat until he brings it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 7. The proof came from people who never bring a כפרה, so maybe it does not apply to people who do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, דבי רבי ישמעאל showed that the פסוק is about a זב with two sightings and a מצורע מוסגר, who have no כפרה to bring. So for them, sunset obviously ends the wait. But that says nothing about someone who must bring a כפרה. Maybe for him, eating תרומה depends on the כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who must bring an atonement קרבן to finish his purification
These words apply (only) to... (limits a rule to a narrower case)
But say... (the גמרא suggests another possibility)

phrases.english: But say: these words apply
to someone who does not need an atonement offering,
phrases.notes: This is the זב with two sightings and the מצורע מוסגר from the last step, who have no קרבן to bring.

phrases.english: but someone who does need an atonement offering
may not eat until he brings his atonement offering?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 7 by limiting it to people with no כפרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from דבי רבי ישמעאל that sunset alone permits תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof only covers people with no כפרה. It cannot show that someone who must bring a כפרה may eat תרומה without it.

steps.title: Where does the three-level rule of the משנה come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a further question: a משנה teaches three stages (טבילה permits מעשר, sunset permits תרומה, כפרה permits קדשים). What is the source for this?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: we learned in a משנה that once he immersed and came up, he may eat מעשר. Once his sun has set, he may eat תרומה. Once he has brought his כפרה, he may eat קדשים. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה listing three stages of becoming טהור and asks for the source in the תורה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ותו' (furthermore) shows that this question adds to the challenge before it. The משנה clearly says that sunset, not the כפרה, permits תרומה, even for someone who needs a כפרה. We still need a פסוק that teaches all three levels.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds another question)
He immersed in a מקוה and came up
His sun has set (the day after his טבילה ended)
Here, מעשר שני, which is eaten in ירושלים
From where do we know this?

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about a person who must bring a כפרה, like a זב or a מצורע who has fully healed. Even so, it says he may eat תרומה after sunset, before his כפרה.

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which we learned in a משנה:
once he immersed and came up, he may eat מעשר;
once his sun has set, he may eat תרומה;
once he has brought his atonement offering, he may eat קדשים.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the challenge of step 8 by asking for the source of a משנה that separates sunset from כפרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוקים that teach the three stages: טבילה for מעשר, sunset for תרומה, and כפרה for קדשים.

steps.title: Three פסוקים, one for each level
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רב חסדא, points to three פסוקים that seem to give three different points of purity, and assigns each one to a different kind of holy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב חסדא: Three פסוקים are written. One says, 'He shall not eat from the holy things unless he bathed his body in water,' so once he bathed, he is טהור. Another says, 'When the sun sets he is טהור, and afterward he may eat from the holy things.' A third says, 'The כהן shall atone for her, and she is טהור.' How can all three be true? One is about מעשר, one is about תרומה, and one is about קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא, quoting רב חסדא, answers the question from step 9. He points to three פסוקים that seem to contradict each other and explains that each one is about a different food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק makes a person טהור right after טבילה, another only after sunset, and a third only after the כפרה. Since all three cannot apply to the same food, each one is assigned to a different level of holiness. This gives a source for the three stages, but it does not yet settle the question of step 8. The גמרא raises that question again in step 16 (ואכתי), and אביי answers it in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Three פסוקים
He bathed his body in water (his טבילה)
And the sun has set
How can this be? (how do we fit the sources together)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not be thrown by the fact that the first two פסוקים both say 'קדשים'. The גמרא spreads the three פסוקים over three kinds of holy food. The plain words do not decide which פסוק goes with which food.
steps.whatToRemember: Three stages for a טמא who becomes טהור: טבילה lets him eat מעשר, sunset lets him eat תרומה, and the כפרה lets him eat קדשים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the three stages of טהרה: מעשר after טבילה, תרומה after sunset, and קדשים after the כפרה. Whether this also covers someone who still owes a כפרה is taken up in steps 16–17.

phrases.english: רבא said that רב חסדא said:
Three פסוקים are written.
It is written: 'And he shall not eat from the holy things'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:6

phrases.english: 'unless he has bathed his body in water,'
so once he has bathed, he is טהור.
And it is written: 'When the sun has set, he is טהור,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:7

phrases.english: 'and afterward he may eat from the holy things.'
And it is written: 'The כהן shall atone for her, and she is טהורה.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:8. This is about a woman after childbirth, who becomes fully טהורה only once her קרבן is brought.

phrases.english: How can this be?

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן לְמַעֲשֵׂר, כָּאן לִתְרוּמָה, כָּאן לְקָדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: This one is for מעשר, this one is for תרומה, and this one is for קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: תְּלָתָא קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question (מנא לן) of step 9. The challenge of step 8 stays open until step 16 repeats it and step 17 answers it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three פסוקים give three points of purity: טבילה for מעשר, sunset for תרומה, and כפרה for קדשים.

steps.title: Why not switch מעשר and תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the order is the other way around, so sunset is needed for מעשר and טבילה alone is enough for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I could reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how רב חסדא matched the פסוקים. Why does sunset go with תרומה and not with מעשר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים themselves do not say which food each one is about. So why not give the easier rule (טבילה alone) to תרומה and the harder rule (sunset) to מעשר?

keyTerms.meaning: But I could reverse it (switch the order)

phrases.english: But I could reverse it!
phrases.notes: He means: let the sunset פסוק be about מעשר, and the bathing פסוק be about תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 10 assigned the פסוקים to מעשר and תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's matching of the sunset פסוק to תרומה and the bathing פסוק to מעשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the פסוקים forces this order, so the opposite order should be just as possible.

steps.title: תרומה is stricter, so it gets the stricter rule
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense for תרומה to need sunset, because תרומה is stricter than מעשר in four ways, remembered by the initials מחפ״ז.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that תרומה is the stricter one, since it has מחפ״ז: מיתה, חומש, פדיון, and זרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the stricter rule belongs to the holier, stricter food, which is תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה has four strict rules that מעשר does not have: מיתה (death by heaven) for eating it on purpose, חומש (an extra fifth) for eating it by mistake, no פדיון (it cannot be redeemed), and it is forbidden to זרים. Since תרומה is more severe, it makes sense that it needs the longer wait until sunset.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is more reasonable
Is stronger or more important (here: stricter)
A memory aid: מִיתָה, חוֹמֶשׁ, פִּדְיוֹן, זָרִים, four strict rules of תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: Holier food needs a higher level of טהרה: מעשר after טבילה, תרומה after sunset (because of מחפ״ז), and קדשים after the כפרה.

phrases.english: It makes sense that תרומה is stricter,
since it has מחפ״ז.
phrases.notes: These are first letters: מיתה, חומש, פדיון, זרים. They are four strict rules that apply to תרומה but not to מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reversal challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reasoning (סברא): the stricter food gets the stricter requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים could be matched either way, so sunset might be needed for מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה is stricter in four ways (מחפ״ז), so it gets the sunset requirement, and מעשר needs only טבילה.

steps.title: On the contrary, tithe is the stricter one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on step 12. מעשר has five strictnesses of its own, remembered by the sign הד״ס ט״ב, so maybe מעשר is the one that should need sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: מעשר is stricter, since it has the five strictnesses of הד״ס ט״ב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason given in step 12 by pointing out that מעשר also has special strictnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said תרומה needs sunset because it has four strictnesses (מחפ״ז). Here the גמרא answers that מעשר has five strictnesses (הד״ס ט״ב). If we just count strictnesses, מעשר looks stricter, so maybe מעשר should be the one that needs sunset.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary: the opposite is true
Stronger or more important; here, stricter
A memory sign for five strictnesses of מעשר: bringing it to ירושלים, the declaration (וידוי), forbidden to a mourner (אונן), rules about טומאה, and removal (ביעור)

phrases.english: On the contrary:
tithe is stricter,
since it has הד״ס ט״ב!
phrases.notes: These letters are a memory sign. Each letter stands for one strict rule that applies to מעשר and not to תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 12 by showing that מעשר also has strictnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that תרומה is stricter than מעשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר has five strictnesses (הד״ס ט״ב) against תרומה's four (מחפ״ז), so the extra requirement of sunset could just as well belong to מעשר.

steps.title: Even so, the death penalty is the weightier strictness
steps.stepSummary: Even though מעשר has more strictnesses, the death penalty connected to תרומה outweighs them, so תרומה is the one that needs sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the death penalty is the weightier strictness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: one strictness of תרומה, the death penalty, is more serious than all five strictnesses of מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a matter of counting strictnesses but of weighing them. The 'מ' of מחפ״ז stands for מיתה, a death penalty (from Heaven). No strictness of מעשר is that severe, so תרומה is still the stricter food and fittingly needs sunset.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
Death: here, the death penalty from Heaven connected to תרומה

phrases.english: Even so,
death is weightier.
phrases.notes: This is the 'מ' of מחפ״ז from step 12: the death penalty from Heaven that goes with תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing strictnesses: one severe strictness outweighs several lighter ones.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מעשר has more strictnesses, maybe it should be the one that needs sunset.
steps.terutzMaskana: The death penalty of תרומה is more serious than all of מעשר's strictnesses, so תרומה needs sunset.

steps.title: רבא: the word 'soul' shows the immersion-only verse is about tithe
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even without the death-penalty argument, the פסוק itself proves it. It says נפש ('any soul'), and the only holy food every Jew may eat is מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even without the argument that death is weightier, you could not say it the other way. The פסוק says 'soul.' What food is the same for every soul? You must say it is מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to step 11's question, taken straight from the wording of the פסוק instead of from comparing strictnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that mentions only טבילה says 'the soul that touches it,' meaning any person. תרומה may be eaten only by כהנים, but מעשר may be eaten by every Jew. So that פסוק must be about מעשר, and the sunset פסוק is left for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say it
Soul, a person: here, any person
You must say: the only possible answer is

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons why תרומה needs sunset while מעשר needs only טבילה: (1) תרומה is stricter because of the death penalty, and (2) רבא's reason: the immersion-only פסוק says נפש, any person, which fits only מעשר.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even without 'death is weightier,'
you still could not say it,
phrases.notes: He means you could not say the reversed order from step 11, that טבילה alone is enough for תרומה.

phrases.english: the verse says: 'soul,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:6

phrases.english: which thing is the same for every soul?
You must say this is tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּלָא מִיתָה עֲדִיפָא, נָמֵי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to step 11, apart from the death-penalty reasoning of steps 12 and 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording of the פסוק itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the strictness argument, maybe the immersion-only פסוק could be about תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word נפש shows that פסוק is about food every Jew eats, which is מעשר.

steps.title: Still, maybe someone who owes an atonement offering must wait for it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back its earlier question: maybe sunset permits תרומה only for someone who has no כפרה to bring, while someone who does owe one must wait until he brings it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still: this rule applies only to someone who does not need a כפרה. But someone who needs a כפרה should have to wait until he brings his כפרה!
steps.whatsHappening: Even with the three פסוקים sorted out, the גמרא repeats the question from step 8 against this source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three פסוקים show that sunset is the point at which תרומה becomes permitted. But that may be true only for a person whose purity is finished at sunset. For a person who also owes a כפרה offering, the source does not yet prove he may eat תרומה before bringing it.

keyTerms.meaning: But still: the problem has not gone away
These words apply only to; this rule is limited to
Someone who needs to bring an atonement offering

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same question as step 8, said again on purpose. The גמרא repeats it because the new source from steps 10–15 still has not answered it.

phrases.english: But still,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָאו בַּר כַּפָּרָה,
phrases.english: this applies only where he does not need atonement,
but where he does need atonement —
not until he brings his atonement!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי, הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָאו בַּר כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the challenge of step 8 and raises it against the three-פסוק source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation in steps 10–15 that sunset permits תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source may cover only people whose purity is finished at sunset. It does not prove that someone who still owes a כפרה may eat תרומה before bringing it.

steps.title: Two verses about a woman after childbirth: one for תרומה, one for holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers step 16 from two פסוקים about a יולדת. 'Until the days of her purification are completed' means she is pure at sunset, and that is for תרומה. 'The כהן shall atone for her and she shall be pure' means she must wait for her קרבן, and that is for קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Two verses are written about a woman after childbirth. One says 'until the days of her purification are completed,' meaning once her days are done she is pure. The other says 'the כהן shall atone for her and she shall be pure,' meaning she is pure only after her קרבן. How do they fit together? One is about תרומה, the other is about קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 16. He shows that a person who still owes a כפרה may eat תרומה after sunset, and he proves it from the two פסוקים about a יולדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים seem to clash, since one makes her pure when her days end and the other only after the כהן atones for her. אביי solves this by giving each פסוק its own area: the sunset פסוק covers תרומה and the כפרה פסוק covers קדשים. A יולדת is the classic מחוסר כפורים, so the same rule applies to everyone who still owes a כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman after childbirth, who must bring קרבנות to finish her purification
The completion of her days of purification
'And the כהן shall atone for her' (through her קרבן)
'How so?' The phrase used to settle two sources that seem to clash
Food from holy offerings (sacrificial meat)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for every מחוסר כפורים: once he immerses and the sun sets, he may eat תרומה, but not קדשים until he brings his קרבן.

phrases.english: אביי said: Two verses are written.
About a woman after childbirth it is written: 'until the days of her purification are completed,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:4

phrases.english: meaning that once her days are completed, she is pure.
And it is written: 'And the priest shall atone for her, and she shall be pure.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:8. This one makes her purity depend on bringing her קרבן.

phrases.english: How so?
Here it is for תרומה, and there it is for sacrificial food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by showing from פסוקים that sunset permits תרומה even for someone who still owes a כפרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting two verses between two areas (תרומה and קדשים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe a מחוסר כפורים must wait for his קרבן even before eating תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sunset פסוק is about תרומה, so a מחוסר כפורים may eat תרומה after sunset. The כפרה פסוק is about קדשים.

steps.title: Why not reverse which verse goes with which food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the sunset פסוק is about קדשים and the כפרה פסוק is about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's split by asking why the two פסוקים could not be matched the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gave each פסוק its own area, but he did not prove which פסוק goes with which. If the matching were reversed, תרומה would need the קרבן and קדשים would need only sunset, which is the opposite result.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But I can reverse it.' A challenge that flips the matching of two sources

phrases.english: But I can reverse it!
phrases.notes: He means: say the sunset פסוק is for קדשים, and the כפרה פסוק is for תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the matching that אביי used in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's matching of the sunset פסוק to תרומה and the כפרה פסוק to קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the split itself decides which פסוק goes with which food, so the reverse matching seems just as possible.

steps.title: Holy offerings are stricter, so they get the stricter rule
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense for קדשים to need the קרבן, because קדשים have six strictnesses, remembered by the initials פנקעכ״ס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable that holy food is stricter, since it has the strictnesses of פנקעכ״ס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 18. The stricter rule (waiting for the קרבן) belongs with the stricter food, which is קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like step 12. Whichever food is stricter in general gets the stricter requirement. קדשים have a list of strictnesses that תרומה does not have, so the כפרה פסוק goes with קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy food is stricter
A memory sign: פיגול, נותר, קרבן, מעילה, כרת, and forbidden to an אונן

phrases.english: It is reasonable that holy food is stricter,
since it has the strictnesses of פנקעכ״ס.
phrases.notes: Each letter stands for one strictness of קדשים: פיגול, נותר, קרבן, מעילה, כרת, and forbidden to an אונן (a mourner on the day of death).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reversal challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reasoning: the stricter food gets the stricter rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The matching could go either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: קדשים are stricter, so they are the ones that need the קרבן.

steps.title: But תרומה has strictnesses too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: תרומה has its own strictnesses, remembered by מחפ״ז, so maybe תרומה should be the stricter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, תרומה is stricter, since it has the strictnesses of מחפ״ז!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 19 by pointing out that תרומה has strictnesses of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same four strictnesses of תרומה from step 12 (מחפ״ז). If תרומה is also strict, it is no longer clear that קדשים should get the stricter rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On the contrary.' Flips the argument around
A memory sign for the four strictnesses of תרומה, mentioned back in step 12

phrases.english: On the contrary, תרומה is stricter,
since it has the strictnesses of מחפ״ז!
phrases.notes: These are the same four strictnesses of תרומה that were listed back in step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 19 that קדשים are the stricter food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה also has its own list of strictnesses, so maybe it is the one that deserves the stricter rule.

steps.title: Holy offerings have more strictnesses
steps.stepSummary: The strictnesses of קדשים (six) are more numerous than those of תרומה (four), so קדשים still count as stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are more numerous!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 20 by counting. קדשים have more strictnesses, so they win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both foods have strict points, but פנקעכ״ס has six items and מחפ״ז has only four. The larger list decides that קדשים are stricter, so the כפרה פסוק goes with them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These are more numerous'

phrases.english: These are more numerous!
phrases.notes: 'These' means the six strictnesses of קדשים, which outnumber the four of תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 and keeps אביי's matching in place.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומה's strictnesses might make it the stricter food.
steps.terutzMaskana: קדשים have more strictnesses, so they are stricter and need the קרבן.

steps.title: רבא proves from the verse itself that the sunset rule is for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says we do not need to count strictnesses. 'And she shall be pure' implies she was still impure before the כפרה, and an impure person can never eat קדשים. So the sunset rule must be about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even without the argument that קדשים have more strictnesses, you could not say otherwise. The פסוק says 'the כהן shall atone for her and she shall be pure,' which shows she was impure until then. If she were allowed קדשים before that, we would apply the פסוק 'the flesh that touches anything impure shall not be eaten.' So learn from this that the sunset rule is about תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a stronger proof for אביי's conclusion. His proof comes straight from the פסוק instead of from counting strictnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'And she shall be pure' tells us that before the כפרה she still had some impurity. The Torah says impure people may not eat קדשים, so it is impossible that she could eat קדשים at sunset, before her כפרה. The only food left for the sunset rule is תרומה, so a מחוסר כפורים may eat תרומה after sunset.

keyTerms.meaning: Without the argument that 'these are more numerous'
By implication; from the wording we can infer
'Apply here this פסוק.' Bring another verse to bear on the case
'Learn from this.' A concluding phrase

steps.whatToRemember: A מחוסר כפורים (like a יולדת after her days are done) may eat תרומה after immersion and sunset, but may not eat קדשים until he brings his קרבן. אביי proves this from two פסוקים plus the greater strictness of קדשים. רבא proves it straight from 'and she shall be pure.'
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not disagree with אביי's conclusion. He agrees that the sunset פסוק is about תרומה. He only replaces the strictness-counting reason with a proof from the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the question of step 16 and repeats the pattern of step 15. There too a proof from the פסוק itself replaced the weighing of strictnesses.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Even without the argument that 'these are more numerous,'
you cannot say it the other way,
because the verse states: 'And the priest shall atone for her, and she shall be pure,'
which implies that until then she is impure.
And if you think the sunset rule is about sacrificial food,
apply here the verse:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל״.
phrases.english: 'And the flesh that touches anything impure shall not be eaten.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:19. If impure contact forbids holy meat, an impure person certainly cannot eat it.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this that it is about תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּלָא הָנָךְ נְפִישָׁן לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reason for the result of steps 17 to 21, using the פסוק instead of the count of strictnesses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that rules out the reversed matching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the count of strictnesses, the reversal from step 18 might seem possible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since she is still impure before the כפרה, and an impure person cannot eat קדשים, the sunset rule must be about תרומה.

steps.title: How can the verse be about תרומה if it includes a convert and a freed maidservant?
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי cites a ברייתא: the word 'אשה' adds a גיורת and a freed שפחה to the יולדת laws. Such women cannot eat תרומה, so the פסוק cannot be about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי objected: Can you really say this פסוק is about תרומה? A ברייתא teaches: 'Speak to the children of Israel.' That would only include Jewish-born women. How do we know a convert and a freed maidservant are included too? Because the פסוק says 'a woman.' But if the פסוק is about תרומה, can a convert or a maidservant ever eat תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא attacks רבא's conclusion from Step 22 that the sunset rule is about תרומה. He uses a ברייתא showing that the same section of the תורה also applies to women who could never eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the word 'אשה' widens the יולדת laws to include a גיורת and a freed שפחה. These women may not marry a כהן, so there seems to be no way they would ever eat תרומה. If the section includes them, a rule in it that is only about תרומה would make no sense for them, so רבא's reading looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it, a sharp challenge to a statement
A woman who converted to Judaism
A non-Jewish maidservant who was freed and became fully Jewish
The פסוק teaches us, introducing the word that proves the point
If you would think, used to show where an idea leads

steps.confusionAlert: רב שישא is not saying a גיורת can't become impure. He is saying that a section of the תורה that includes her can't have a rule about eating תרומה, because she seemingly never eats תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, objected to this:
And can you really say
that teruma is written about here?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פסוק about waiting until the days of her purity are finished (ויקרא 12:4), which רבא said is about תרומה.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
"Speak to the children of Israel,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:2

phrases.english: from this I would know only about the children of Israel;
from where do we know a convert and a freed maidservant?
The verse says: "A woman."
phrases.notes: The general word 'woman' in the same פסוק widens the law to include any woman.

phrases.english: And if you think it is about teruma,
a convert and a maidservant,
are they women who can eat teruma?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's conclusion in Step 22 that the sunset rule is about תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of אביי, backed by רבא, that the פסוק 'until the days of her purity are completed' (ויקרא 12:4) refers to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא includes a גיורת and a freed שפחה in this section. They seemingly can never eat תרומה, so a rule here about תרומה would not fit them.

steps.title: רבא questions the assumption that these women can never eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with a short question: 'And can't they?' He rejects the idea that a גיורת and a freed שפחה could never be eligible for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And are they really not able to eat תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the hidden assumption in רב שישא's challenge. This short line sets up an explanation that will show how these women could come to eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שישא's whole challenge rests on one assumption: that a גיורת and a freed שפחה are never eligible for תרומה. רבא attacks that assumption directly instead of giving up his reading of the פסוק. If such women can sometimes eat תרומה, including them in the section is no problem, and רבא's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And not?', a short rhetorical question that rejects the other side's assumption

steps.confusionAlert: 'ולא?' is not a doubt or a real question. It is רבא's way of saying 'Who says they can't?' The details of how come next.

phrases.english: Rava said: And are they not?
phrases.notes: He means: who says a convert or freed maidservant can never eat תרומה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שישא's challenge in Step 23 by rejecting its basic assumption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the premise of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גיורת and a freed שפחה can never eat תרומה, so the פסוק cannot be about תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא denies that they are never eligible for תרומה, so his reading can still stand. The explanation comes next.
